title: Linear Algebra
summary: The highest-yield maths area in GATE DA: expect 4–6 questions (many MSQ/NAT) on rank/nullity, eigenvalues, projection/rank-1 matrices (uu^T, I - 11^T/n) and singular values. Questions reward structural insight (eigenvalues of special matrices, rank arguments) far more than heavy computation.
notesGuide: 1) Download the free 'Mathematics for Machine Learning' PDF (mml-book.github.io/book/mml-book.pdf) and print Ch 2 (Linear Algebra), Ch 3 (Analytic Geometry: projections, orthogonality) and Ch 4 (Matrix Decompositions: det, eigen, Cholesky, SVD) - this matches the DA syllabus almost exactly. 2) Follow MIT 18.06 lectures and download the per-lecture summary + problem-set PDFs from the 18.06SC session pages (each session has a lecture summary, problems and solutions). 3) Keep Strang's free ILA 6th-edition chapter solutions (math.mit.edu/~gs/linearalgebra/ila6/ chXXasols.pdf) and SVD_Slides.pdf for revision. 4) Use Uday Khankhoje's IIT Madras EE5120 web notes (ee.iitm.ac.in/~uday/notes/linalg/) as a compact second reading. 5) Make your own 4–5 page 'formula + trap' sheet: rank-nullity, rank(AB)<=min, rank(A^TA)=rank(A), trace=sum eig, det=product eig, eigenvalues of A^k, A^-1, A+cI, uu^T (eigs: ||u||^2,0,...), projection P=A(A^TA)^-1A^T (P^2=P, P^T=P, eig 0/1), orthogonal Q (|eig|=1, det ±1), idempotent (rank=trace), block-matrix det/inverse rules, quadratic form definiteness tests, SVD (singular values = sqrt eig of A^TA). Add every PYQ you get wrong as a one-line trap to this sheet.

topics.title: Vector Spaces, Subspaces & Linear Independence
subtopics: Column space, null space, row space, left null space (four fundamental subspaces)
topics.tips: For 'is this a subspace?' check the zero vector first and look for non-linear constraints (x^2, |x|, x+y=1). Independence of k vectors = rank of the matrix formed is k.

topics.title: Systems of Linear Equations & Gaussian Elimination
subtopics: Homogeneous systems, number of free variables
topics.tips: Unique iff rank = number of unknowns; infinite iff consistent and rank < n. If Ax=b has a unique solution for some b, A has full column rank, so Ax=c has at most one solution for every c.

topics.title: Rank, Nullity & Determinant
subtopics: Rank (row/column), rank of products and sums
topics.tips: rank(A^TA)=rank(A); rank(AB) <= min(rank A, rank B). det(kA)=k^n det(A) for n x n - a classic trap. Spot linearly dependent rows (row3=row1+row2) before computing.

topics.title: Eigenvalues & Eigenvectors
subtopics: Trace = sum, det = product of eigenvalues
Eigenvalues of A^k, A^-1, A+cI, A^T, triangular matrices
Symmetric matrices: real eigenvalues, orthogonal eigenvectors
topics.tips: Never expand a 3x3 characteristic polynomial if trace/det/structure suffices. Real 2x2 matrices can have complex eigenvalues (check discriminant). Use Cayley-Hamilton for expressions like |M^2 + 12M|.

topics.title: Orthogonality, Projections & Least Squares
subtopics: Projection onto a line and a subspace
Projection matrix P = A(A^TA)^-1A^T, P^2=P, P^T=P
topics.tips: A projection onto a k-dim subspace of R^n has eigenvalues 1 (k times) and 0 (n-k times), rank k, trace k, and is singular unless k=n. I-P projects onto the orthogonal complement.

topics.title: Quadratic Forms & Positive Definiteness
subtopics: x^T A x and symmetric representation
Positive/negative (semi)definite tests: eigenvalues, leading minors, pivots
Max/min of x^T A x on unit sphere (Rayleigh quotient)
topics.tips: max x^TAx subject to ||x||=1 equals the largest eigenvalue of the symmetric part of A. Always symmetrise A first: x^TAx = x^T((A+A^T)/2)x.

topics.title: LU Decomposition
subtopics: When LU exists (nonzero pivots) vs PA = LU
topics.tips: Entries of L below the diagonal are the elimination multipliers; L has 1s on its diagonal (Doolittle). A zero pivot means row exchange is needed (PA=LU).

topics.title: Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)
subtopics: Rank = number of nonzero singular values
Low-rank approximation, link to PCA, pseudoinverse
topics.tips: For symmetric PSD matrices (e.g. uu^T, projections) singular values equal eigenvalues; for general symmetric matrices they are absolute eigenvalues. Sum of singular values of uu^T = ||u||^2.
